facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Leverage rose because earnings fell while debt stayed near USD 6,852 million. Total debt over reported EBITDA was 5.54x for FY2025 and is 8.46x on the last twelve months, as EBITDA fell from USD 1,176 million to USD 810 million while operating profit fell from USD 838 million to USD 428 million. The reported measures carry one-offs: the last twelve months include gains on disposals of USD 389 million and restructuring costs of USD 154 million. Excluding both, an Analyst Judgement measure, EBITDA is USD 681 million and net debt is 8.44x of it. Basis: calculation C65; calculation C71; calculation C18; calculation C42; calculation C39; calculation C91; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7; 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 75–77

rows.label: Chart data: revenue and EBITDA — paragraph 1

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- The instrument-level debt table is printed only for 2025-12-31, so debt by instrument, maturity and carrying value after the June 2026 refinancing is not established; it restricts the maturity chart, the debt stack and the refinancing view, and the later ladder must be rebuilt and labelled as built. Severity: High. Action: supply an instrument-level debt schedule at 2026-09-30. - Cash paid for interest is printed for FY2024 and FY2025 only, so cash interest cover for 2026 periods and the last twelve months is not calculable and income statement interest expense is used only as a labelled proxy. Severity: High. Action: supply 2026 supplemental cash flow disclosures. - ABL borrowing-base availability and letters of credit drawn on the facility are not stated, so undrawn committed facilities of USD 2,193 million may overstate usable liquidity. Severity: High. Action: supply the latest borrowing base certificate or a statement of availability and letters of credit by facility. - The ABL maturity date and the covenant levels other than the springing fixed charge coverage minimum are not stated, which restricts the liquidity runway view. Severity: Medium. Action: supply the executed credit agreement. - The issuer states no EBITDA or adjusted EBITDA figure, so reported EBITDA is derived from operating profit and depreciation and amortisation, and no adjusted EBITDA row or bridge is stated; the Analyst Judgement measure fills the gap only as a labelled house view. Severity: Medium. Action: supply an issuer adjusted EBITDA reconciliation if one exists. - Total liabilities at 2026-06-30 is left unsupplied because the printed current liabilities, noncurrent liabilities and equity add to 17,325 against total assets of 17,326; the filing itself prints the difference. Severity: Low. Action: none beyond noting the rounding. - The printed net change in cash differs by 1 from its components or from opening and closing cash for FY2024, the first quarter of 2026 and the first half of 2025, so Net Cash Change is left unsupplied in those columns. Severity: Low. Action: none beyond noting the rounding. - Several income statement lines differ by 1 from their printed subtotals in some periods, which is rounding in the filings and is not corrected. Severity: Low. Action: none. - Cash flow statements print year-to-date periods only, so discrete second and third quarter depreciation and amortisation is derived by subtraction and labelled calculated, and the stand-alone fourth quarter of 2025 is not carried. Severity: Low. Action: supply the fourth-quarter release if a discrete quarter is wanted. - FY2023 income statement and cash flow figures are printed in the annual report but are not carried here because no balance sheet at 2023-12-31 is in the set. Severity: Low. Action: none unless a FY2023 leverage point is wanted. - Lines printed as a dash in a statement (for example the noncontrolling interest line in some 2026 quarters and the current maturities line at 2026-09-30) are carried as not supplied, not as zero; the filing states 14 of debt due within twelve months, which supports the total debt used. Severity: Low. Action: none. - Supplier finance confirmed obligations at 2025-12-31 are 763 in the annual report and 772 as the opening balance of the 2026 quarterly reports, a difference of 9 that the sources do not explain. Severity: Medium. Action: ask the issuer which figure stands. - The rank of the Brazil committed facilities and of notes payable, the security (if any) of the older senior notes, the currency of the Brazil facilities and the principal amounts of most senior notes are not stated, so those facilities are left out of the debt stack and several instrument cells are unsupplied. Severity: Medium. Action: supply the indenture and facility documents. - Segment net sales and EBIT are carried for FY2024, FY2025, the third quarter and nine months; the first and second quarters and the 2025 half-year are not carried. Severity: Low. Action: none unless those quarters are wanted. - Cash paid for income taxes is printed for fiscal years only, so 2026 cash taxes are not established. Severity: Low. Action: supply 2026 supplemental cash flow disclosures.

facts.label: Overall governance view
facts.text: Overall, Whirlpool presents Medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is a suspended common dividend, USD 1,081 million of net equity and a secured refinancing that removed near-term maturities, which matters because it cut liquidity risk while placing secured claims ahead of unsecured creditors and implies lower default risk but higher loss given default for unsecured creditors. Countervailing evidence is the 2025 distributions above free cash flow, the May 2026 covenant amendment and the Brazil contingencies. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the executed debt documents and the security status of the older notes. - The 2026 proxy statement was not supplied, so directors, committees, independence, holders above 5%, executive pay and the related-party approval policy are not established; this restricts the governance and ownership findings. Severity: High. Action: obtain the proxy statement. - The executed asset-based credit agreement, the second-lien indenture and the certificate of designations were not supplied, only the issuer's summaries, so restricted-payment, debt and lien capacity, the facility maturity and the covenant levels other than the springing fixed charge test are not established. Severity: High. Action: obtain the exhibits to the Form 8-K of June 16, 2026. - Whether the older unsecured senior notes share the new liens is not stated, so the ranking of unsecured creditors against USD 4,000 million of secured capacity cannot be settled. Severity: High. Action: obtain the indentures and the permitted lien terms. - Borrowing-base availability, letters of credit, compliance certificates and basket usage are not available, so covenant headroom cannot be monitored from the filings. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the lender reporting package. - Where the proceeds of the sale-leasebacks and of the India and Beko Europe sales went is not stated, so how far disposals reduced debt is not established. Severity: Medium. Action: ask management for the use of proceeds. - The funding source of the USD 300 million of dividends paid in 2025 is not stated. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the 2025 funding reconciliation. - Sponsor items such as fund vintage, life left, entry multiple, sponsor fees and veto rights are not disclosed because no sponsor is named, and they are not inferred. Severity: Low. Action: none unless a controlling holder is identified. - The sales split by product category is a chart not carried in the text read. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the chart data from the annual report. - The S&P rating after February 2026 is not stated, and the dates of the second-quarter 2026 Moody's and Fitch downgrades within the quarter are not given. Severity: Low. Action: obtain current rating agency reports. - The termination date of the private placement and the purpose of the June 23, 2026 deed of amendment to the European contribution agreement are not stated. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the related Form 8-K filings. - Supplier finance at year-end 2025 is 763 in the annual report and 772 as the opening balance in the 2026 quarterly reports; the 9 difference is not explained. Severity: Low. Action: ask the issuer which balance stands.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Leverage is high and rose as earnings fell, so the February equity raise bought time rather than repair. Net debt of USD 5,749 million is 7.10x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA of USD 810 million, against 4.98x at year-end 2025, and 8.44x on EBITDA of USD 681 million excluding one-offs. Net debt fell only USD 102 million since year-end 2025 despite USD 1,081 million of net equity, while EBITDA fell USD 366 million, or 31.12%. Cash interest cover was 3.36x in 2025; no 2026 cash interest figure is printed, and third-quarter interest expense of USD 102 million annualises to cover of 1.99x. facts.text: The asset-based facility and the second-lien notes are guaranteed by the domestic and Canadian subsidiaries that are obligors under the facility. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Whirlpool presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, brands, domestic manufacturing behind a 25% import tariff and a small domestic appliance segment earning an 18.6% EBIT margin, but credit quality is constrained by leverage of 7.10x EBITDA, negative free cash flow, concentration in North America and one customer, and secured debt that ranks ahead of the older unsecured notes unless they share it. Cash-flow durability appears weak due to a first half of outflows, a fourth-quarter release that must reach USD 1,526 million and margins that have not yet recovered. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on delivery of the fourth-quarter cash inflow, the recovery of North American margins in 2027 and ratings of Ba3 at Moody's, BB- at Fitch and BB with a negative outlook at S&P. The primary downside path is a fourth-quarter shortfall that leaves net debt near USD 4,760 million, a seasonal first-quarter outflow on a shrinking borrowing base and a springing covenant that warns late. Further analysis would require borrowing-base availability, the executed debt documents, the proxy statement, instrument-level debt after June 2026, cash interest paid in 2026 and peer data. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3; calculation C24; calculation C29; calculation C14

# CP-1 Financial foundation: WHIRLPOOL CORP /DE/ (whr)
## Request

This is the financial foundation for WHIRLPOOL CORP /DE/ (whr), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. It states the consolidated statements for FY2024, FY2025 and the 2026 interim periods through the third quarter, the debt and liquidity tables, and the leverage and cover measures built from them. All amounts are consolidated Whirlpool Corporation, in millions of US dollars unless a row says otherwise.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Reported leverage is high and rising: net debt of USD 5,749 million is 7.10x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA of USD 810 million at 2026-09-30, so creditors depend on liquidity and asset sales rather than earnings to service debt.
Basis: calculation C55; calculation C24; calculation C72; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7

Cash of USD 1,103 million and USD 2,193 million of undrawn committed facilities, before an unstated borrowing-base cap, are set against only USD 14 million of debt due within twelve months. Cash interest paid for 2026 and a debt table by instrument after the June 2026 refinancing are not printed, so interest cover is stated for fiscal years only.
Basis: calculation C79; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 77
### Key findings

Leverage rose because earnings fell while debt stayed near USD 6,852 million. Total debt over reported EBITDA was 5.54x for FY2025 and is 8.46x on the last twelve months, as EBITDA fell from USD 1,176 million to USD 810 million while operating profit fell from USD 838 million to USD 428 million. The reported measures carry one-offs: the last twelve months include gains on disposals of USD 389 million and restructuring costs of USD 154 million. Excluding both, an Analyst Judgement measure, EBITDA is USD 681 million and net debt is 8.44x of it.

Basis: calculation C65; calculation C71; calculation C18; calculation C42; calculation C39; calculation C91; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7; 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 75–77

Interest cover on cash interest paid was 3.36x for FY2025, against 1.35x for FY2024. No cash interest figure is printed for any 2026 period, so cover on a cash basis cannot be stated for the last twelve months. Income statement interest expense of USD 326 million gives a proxy cover of 2.48x. After the June 2026 refinancing, third-quarter interest expense was USD 102 million, an annual rate of USD 408 million, which would be 1.99x of last-twelve-months EBITDA (a derived illustration, not a reported figure).
Basis: calculation C74; calculation C73; calculation C89; calculation C88; calculation C90; 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5

Cash flow is the pressure point. Operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 826 million in the nine months of 2026, against an outflow of USD 669 million a year earlier, and free cash flow after capital expenditure of USD 255 million was an outflow of USD 1,081 million. Payables fell by USD 306 million and accrued advertising and promotions by USD 318 million, the seasonal unwind of supplier and customer funding that lower earnings did not replace. The February 2026 equity issuance of USD 1,081 million net and asset sales funded the outflow, not operations.
Basis: calculation C85; calculation C87; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-03-31_whr-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7

Liquidity at 2026-09-30 was USD 1,103 million of cash and USD 2,193 million of undrawn commitments, USD 3,296 million together, before any cap from the borrowing base and before letters of credit, neither of which is stated. The new asset-based facility cut undrawn commitments by USD 1,239 million from year-end 2025, when the previous revolver left USD 3,432 million undrawn. Cash of USD 1,239 million at 2026-06-30 included USD 212 million restricted for the July 1, 2026 debt payment.

Basis: calculation C80; calculation C81; calculation C76; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; EX-99.1_2026-08-03_exhibit991pressrelease0630.htm.jsonl, page 8

The year-end 2025 maturity ladder, USD 6,168 million of contractual maturities including USD 586 million in 2026 and USD 702 million in 2027, no longer describes the debt. The June 2026 refinancing repaid the 2026 and 2027 notes and the unsecured revolver with two USD 1,000 million second-lien issues and borrowings under the new facility. The balance sheet now shows USD 14 million of debt due within twelve months, but the instrument-level table after the refinancing is not printed, so the maturity ladder here is drawn at year-end 2025 and the later profile must be rebuilt and labelled as built.
Basis: calculation C61; 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 100–101; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6

Definitions matter for every ratio here. The issuer states no EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is operating profit plus depreciation and amortisation, which keeps restructuring, impairments and disposal gains in it. Debt is balance-sheet carrying value including notes payable, with lease liabilities and supplier finance kept outside it. Supplier finance obligations of USD 650 million at 2026-09-30 sit in accounts payable, and the 2025 annual report prints USD 763 million at year-end 2025 where the 2026 quarterly reports open at USD 772 million.

## Gaps

- The instrument-level debt table is printed only for 2025-12-31, so debt by instrument, maturity and carrying value after the June 2026 refinancing is not established; it restricts the maturity chart, the debt stack and the refinancing view, and the later ladder must be rebuilt and labelled as built. Severity: High. Action: supply an instrument-level debt schedule at 2026-09-30.

- Cash paid for interest is printed for FY2024 and FY2025 only, so cash interest cover for 2026 periods and the last twelve months is not calculable and income statement interest expense is used only as a labelled proxy. Severity: High. Action: supply 2026 supplemental cash flow disclosures.

- ABL borrowing-base availability and letters of credit drawn on the facility are not stated, so undrawn committed facilities of USD 2,193 million may overstate usable liquidity. Severity: High. Action: supply the latest borrowing base certificate or a statement of availability and letters of credit by facility.

- The ABL maturity date and the covenant levels other than the springing fixed charge coverage minimum are not stated, which restricts the liquidity runway view. Severity: Medium. Action: supply the executed credit agreement.

- The issuer states no EBITDA or adjusted EBITDA figure, so reported EBITDA is derived from operating profit and depreciation and amortisation, and no adjusted EBITDA row or bridge is stated; the Analyst Judgement measure fills the gap only as a labelled house view. Severity: Medium. Action: supply an issuer adjusted EBITDA reconciliation if one exists.

- Total liabilities at 2026-06-30 is left unsupplied because the printed current liabilities, noncurrent liabilities and equity add to 17,325 against total assets of 17,326; the filing itself prints the difference. Severity: Low. Action: none beyond noting the rounding.

- The printed net change in cash differs by 1 from its components or from opening and closing cash for FY2024, the first quarter of 2026 and the first half of 2025, so Net Cash Change is left unsupplied in those columns. Severity: Low. Action: none beyond noting the rounding.
- Several income statement lines differ by 1 from their printed subtotals in some periods, which is rounding in the filings and is not corrected. Severity: Low. Action: none.

- Cash flow statements print year-to-date periods only, so discrete second and third quarter depreciation and amortisation is derived by subtraction and labelled calculated, and the stand-alone fourth quarter of 2025 is not carried. Severity: Low. Action: supply the fourth-quarter release if a discrete quarter is wanted.

- FY2023 income statement and cash flow figures are printed in the annual report but are not carried here because no balance sheet at 2023-12-31 is in the set. Severity: Low. Action: none unless a FY2023 leverage point is wanted.

- Lines printed as a dash in a statement (for example the noncontrolling interest line in some 2026 quarters and the current maturities line at 2026-09-30) are carried as not supplied, not as zero; the filing states 14 of debt due within twelve months, which supports the total debt used. Severity: Low. Action: none.

- Supplier finance confirmed obligations at 2025-12-31 are 763 in the annual report and 772 as the opening balance of the 2026 quarterly reports, a difference of 9 that the sources do not explain. Severity: Medium. Action: ask the issuer which figure stands.

- The rank of the Brazil committed facilities and of notes payable, the security (if any) of the older senior notes, the currency of the Brazil facilities and the principal amounts of most senior notes are not stated, so those facilities are left out of the debt stack and several instrument cells are unsupplied. Severity: Medium. Action: supply the indenture and facility documents.

- Segment net sales and EBIT are carried for FY2024, FY2025, the third quarter and nine months; the first and second quarters and the 2025 half-year are not carried. Severity: Low. Action: none unless those quarters are wanted.
- Cash paid for income taxes is printed for fiscal years only, so 2026 cash taxes are not established. Severity: Low. Action: supply 2026 supplemental cash flow disclosures.

# CP-1A Business & governance: WHIRLPOOL CORP /DE/ (whr)
## Request

This is the business and governance assessment for WHIRLPOOL CORP /DE/ (whr), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. It covers the business and operating model, ownership, transactions and capital allocation, issuer history and the governance and financial-policy behaviour that bears on creditors. Amounts are consolidated Whirlpool Corporation in millions of US dollars unless a row says otherwise.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Whirlpool is a listed appliance maker with no sponsor or controlling holder named in the filings read, and its 2026 financial policy has favoured creditors, but weak earnings and new secured debt leave unsecured creditors dependent on a large fourth-quarter cash recovery.

Management suspended the common dividend, raised USD 1,081 million of net equity in February and took USD 254 million of proceeds from asset sales in the nine months. The June 2026 refinancing put USD 2,000 million of second-lien notes and a USD 2,000 million asset-based facility on the main asset pool, and whether the older unsecured notes share that security is not established. Board, holder and related-party detail sits in a proxy statement that was not supplied.
Basis: calculation C18; calculation C29; calculation C27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–22; 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 2
### Key findings

Creditor risk here comes from management's own financial policy, not from a sponsor, because no sponsor or controlling holder is named. The annual report takes director and ownership information from a proxy statement that was not supplied, so who holds the votes and how the board is composed are not established. Common shares outstanding rose 16.31% from February to October 2026 after the equity raise, and the new mandatory convertible preferred converts into common stock in February 2029, adding 10.79% to 12.68% to the October share count, so it is a cash cost of about USD 48.88 million a year until then and not a maturity.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-03-31_whr-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C15; calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C25

The business is a North American appliance franchise with one large customer, which explains both its cash generation and this year's earnings fall. MDA North America was 65.43% of 2025 net sales and the United States alone 65.06%; Lowe's took about 15% of net sales and was about 44% of receivables at year-end. Latin America was 21.08% and small domestic appliances 7.14%, the latter earning an 18.6% EBIT margin in the third quarter of 2026. The product-category split is a chart not carried in the text read, so dependence on laundry, refrigeration or cooking is not established.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 4–10; 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 132; 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 133; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_exhibit991pressrelease0930.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C13

Earnings fell in 2026 mostly on volume, tariffs and cost inflation in North America, and the recovery management describes is announced rather than visible. Nine-month net sales fell 8.39%, of which 72.37% sits in the Other column that held the former Asia business; MDA North America sales fell 5.87% and its EBIT fell 66.36%, to a margin of 2.0% from 5.6%. Management calls the pace of recovery slower than expected and guides the 2026 ongoing EBIT margin to 2.0% to 2.2%, against 4.7% in 2025, leaning on price increases of 7% in North America and up to 10% in Latin America from the fourth quarter.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 47–49; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_exhibit991pressrelease0930.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C12

Year-end deleveraging depends on a fourth-quarter cash inflow that management's own guidance puts at USD 1,526 million. Operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 826 million in nine months, the full-year guidance is about USD 700 million, and net debt of USD 5,749 million at 2026-09-30 has to fall by USD 1,249 million to meet the target of below USD 4,500 million. Net debt fell only USD 102 million from year-end 2025 despite the USD 1,081 million equity raise, and revenue and margins are typically highest in the third and fourth quarters, which supports the pattern but not the size.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against a cautious view is that management has already acted on most levers. Dividends are suspended, USD 1,081 million of equity was raised, the USD 2,000 million asset-based facility was undrawn at 2026-09-30, cash was USD 1,103 million and only USD 14 million of debt falls due within twelve months, which gives liquidity of USD 3,296 million before any borrowing-base cap. The weakness also has identifiable causes in tariffs, soft North American demand and a customer bankruptcy, while small domestic appliances held an 18.6% EBIT margin and price increases of 7% and up to 10% are announced.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_exhibit991pressrelease0930.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; calculation C18; calculation C45

The view would improve if fourth-quarter cash flow brings net debt below USD 4,500 million, if the proxy statement shows an independent board and no related-party leakage, and if the executed documents show that the older notes share the new security or that restricted-payment capacity is small. It would worsen if the fourth-quarter inflow falls short, if a further covenant amendment or waiver is needed, if dividends or buybacks resume before net debt falls, or if the India, China or Arcelik stakes are sold below the USD 674 million at which they stood at 2026-09-30.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-26_exhibit991pressrelease0930.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–22; calculation C44; calculation C34
### Limitations

- The proxy statement was not supplied, so board composition, independence, any holder above 5%, executive pay and the related-party approval policy are not established; the finding that creditor risk comes from management policy rather than a holder could change if one holder controls the votes.

- Only the issuer's summaries of the asset-based facility and the second-lien indenture were read, so restricted-payment, debt and lien capacity, the facility maturity and the ranking of the older unsecured notes are not established; the conclusion that covenants limit leakage could be weaker than stated.
- Fourth-quarter cash flow and year-end net debt are management guidance and a derived arithmetic gap, not reported results; the deleveraging conclusion holds only if that guidance is met.
- The sales split by product category is not carried in the text read, so the business concentration conclusion rests on segment, country and customer figures only.

- Segment figures for 2025 include the former Asia business until its deconsolidation in November 2025, so year-on-year segment changes mix a changing perimeter and the share of the 2026 sales fall attributed to the Other column is approximate.

- Nothing after 2026-10-27 is read, so the effect of the fourth-quarter price increases, any later rating action and the date the private placement ended are not established; each could shift the earnings-recovery conclusion either way.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Whirlpool's 2026 funding changed in three steps. In February it sold common stock and 8.50% mandatory convertible preferred stock for USD 1,081 million net and used about USD 900 million to repay part of its revolving credit facility. In May it amended that facility, dropping the first-quarter interest coverage test and cutting commitments from USD 3,500 million to USD 2,250 million, with refinancing required before July 1. On June 16 it replaced the facility with a USD 2,000 million asset-based facility and issued USD 2,000 million of second-lien notes in two equal series due 2031 and 2034.

The asset-based facility and the second-lien notes are guaranteed by each domestic and Canadian subsidiary that is an obligor under the facility. The facility has first-priority liens and the notes second-priority liens on the same collateral pool of eligible accounts receivable, inventory, intellectual property and machinery and equipment. The facility carries a springing fixed charge coverage test of 1.00x that applies when availability falls below the greater of 10% of the line cap and USD 135 million. Nothing was drawn on it at 2026-09-30, and borrowing-base availability and letters of credit are not stated.

The proceeds paid for the 2026 and 2027 senior notes issued by a wholly owned subsidiary and, with borrowings under the new facility, repaid the previous unsecured revolver; the remaining USD 212 million of those notes was discharged on July 1, 2026. The second-lien notes cost USD 153.75 million a year in coupons. The financing note does not describe the other senior notes listed in the annual report as repaid, and the filings do not say whether they were secured equally with the new debt.

A USD 30 million private placement of common stock to a subsidiary of Whirlpool China was agreed in February and ended because regulatory approvals were not obtained.

Sponsor and governance risk level: Medium.

The risk level is driven by distributions above free cash flow in 2025, a covenant amendment under stress in May 2026 and USD 2,000 million of second-lien notes placed ahead of unsecured creditors, because these show a willingness to use the balance sheet and security to defend liquidity, which implies higher loss given default for unsecured creditors if earnings do not recover. ### Overall governance view

Overall, Whirlpool presents Medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is a suspended common dividend, USD 1,081 million of net equity and a secured refinancing that removed near-term maturities, which matters because it cut liquidity risk while placing secured claims ahead of unsecured creditors and implies lower default risk but higher loss given default for unsecured creditors. Countervailing evidence is the 2025 distributions above free cash flow, the May 2026 covenant amendment and the Brazil contingencies. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the executed debt documents and the security status of the older notes.

## Gaps

- The 2026 proxy statement was not supplied, so directors, committees, independence, holders above 5%, executive pay and the related-party approval policy are not established; this restricts the governance and ownership findings. Severity: High. Action: obtain the proxy statement.

- The executed asset-based credit agreement, the second-lien indenture and the certificate of designations were not supplied, only the issuer's summaries, so restricted-payment, debt and lien capacity, the facility maturity and the covenant levels other than the springing fixed charge test are not established. Severity: High. Action: obtain the exhibits to the Form 8-K of June 16, 2026.

- Whether the older unsecured senior notes share the new liens is not stated, so the ranking of unsecured creditors against USD 4,000 million of secured capacity cannot be settled. Severity: High. Action: obtain the indentures and the permitted lien terms.

- Borrowing-base availability, letters of credit, compliance certificates and basket usage are not available, so covenant headroom cannot be monitored from the filings. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the lender reporting package.

- Where the proceeds of the sale-leasebacks and of the India and Beko Europe sales went is not stated, so how far disposals reduced debt is not established. Severity: Medium. Action: ask management for the use of proceeds.
- The funding source of the USD 300 million of dividends paid in 2025 is not stated. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the 2025 funding reconciliation.

- Sponsor items such as fund vintage, life left, entry multiple, sponsor fees and veto rights are not disclosed because no sponsor is named, and they are not inferred. Severity: Low. Action: none unless a controlling holder is identified.
- The sales split by product category is a chart not carried in the text read. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the chart data from the annual report.

- The S&P rating after February 2026 is not stated, and the dates of the second-quarter 2026 Moody's and Fitch downgrades within the quarter are not given. Severity: Low. Action: obtain current rating agency reports.

- The termination date of the private placement and the purpose of the June 23, 2026 deed of amendment to the European contribution agreement are not stated. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the related Form 8-K filings.

- Supplier finance at year-end 2025 is 763 in the annual report and 772 as the opening balance in the 2026 quarterly reports; the 9 difference is not explained. Severity: Low. Action: ask the issuer which balance stands.

# CP-2 Fundamental credit: WHIRLPOOL CORP /DE/ (whr)
## Request

This is the fundamental credit assessment for WHIRLPOOL CORP /DE/ (whr), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. It synthesises the financial foundation, the business and governance assessment and the issuer's own filings into the credit's strengths, constraints, downside path and monitoring triggers. Amounts are consolidated Whirlpool Corporation in millions of US dollars unless a row says otherwise.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Whirlpool's credit is weak and deteriorating but liquid: net debt of 7.10x last-twelve-months EBITDA and negative free cash flow leave creditors reliant on a fourth-quarter cash inflow that guidance sets well above last year's.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3; calculation C10; calculation C24; calculation C22

Liquidity of USD 3,296 million before any borrowing-base cap and only USD 14 million of debt due within twelve months make a near-term shortfall unlikely, but management cut its margin outlook by 2.0 percentage points to 1.8 percentage points in twelve weeks while keeping its cash target, and the June refinancing put USD 2,000 million of second-lien notes and a USD 2,000 million asset-based facility on the main asset pool ahead of unsecured claims on it.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C9; calculation C37; calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; EX-99.1_2026-08-03_exhibit991pressrelease0630.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_exhibit991pressrelease0930.htm.jsonl, page 2
### Key findings

Leverage is high and rose as earnings fell, so the February equity raise bought time rather than repair. Net debt of USD 5,749 million is 7.10x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA of USD 810 million, against 4.98x at year-end 2025, and 8.44x on EBITDA of USD 681 million excluding one-offs. Net debt fell only USD 102 million since year-end 2025 despite USD 1,081 million of net equity, while EBITDA fell USD 366 million, or 31.12%. Cash interest cover was 3.36x in 2025; no 2026 cash interest figure is printed, and third-quarter interest expense of USD 102 million annualises to cover of 1.99x.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C8

Year-end deleveraging rests on a working-capital release rather than on earnings. Guidance of about USD 700 million of operating cash flow for 2026 implies USD 1,526 million in the fourth quarter, USD 387 million or 33.98% more than the USD 1,139 million of the fourth quarter of 2025, while the guided margin implies fourth-quarter ongoing EBIT of USD 87 million to USD 116 million, below USD 135 million a year earlier. Reaching the net debt target of below USD 4,500 million needs a reduction of USD 1,249 million; if fourth-quarter free cash flow only repeats last year's USD 989 million, net debt would be about USD 4,760 million, USD 260 million above the target. Management cut its margin outlook but kept the cash target and lowered the net debt target by USD 500 million.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-03_exhibit991pressrelease0630.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_exhibit991pressrelease0930.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_exhibit991pressrelease0930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C24; calculation C26; calculation C22; calculation C33; calculation C34; calculation C28; calculation C23; calculation C29; calculation C39

Near-term liquidity is the main support, but its usable size is not stated. Cash of USD 1,103 million and undrawn facilities of USD 2,193 million give USD 3,296 million, 3.99x the USD 827 million operating cash outflow of the first quarter of 2026, with USD 14 million of debt due within twelve months and management stating that maturities are cleared until 2028. The asset-based facility is limited by a borrowing base, availability and letters of credit are not stated, bank guarantees, letters of credit and surety bonds stood at USD 578 million, and the fixed charge test springs when availability falls below the greater of 10% of the line cap and USD 135 million.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 58; EX-99.1_2026-08-03_exhibit991pressrelease0630.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_exhibit991pressrelease0930.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-03-31_whr-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C9; calculation C44; calculation C47; calculation C45

The business has scale and brands, but price has not yet offset volume, tariffs and cost inflation, so margins fell faster than sales. MDA North America, 65.43% of 2025 sales, lost USD 445 million of nine-month sales and USD 284 million of EBIT, 63.82% of the lost sales, as volume, tariffs and cost inflation outweighed price; its EBIT margin was 2.0% against 5.6%, and the group's last-twelve-months gross margin was 13.08% against 15.37% in 2025. Sequential progress is real, with ongoing EBIT margin of 1.3%, 1.8% and 2.6% over the three quarters, but management attributes it to price increases and cost take-out, not volume.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 47–49; EX-99.1_2026-05-06_exhibit991pressrelease0331.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-08-03_exhibit991pressrelease0630.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_exhibit991pressrelease0930.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C18; calculation C41; calculation C40

Cash conversion is the weakest dimension. Free cash flow was USD 81 million in 2025, 6.89% of EBITDA against 80.67% in 2024, and negative USD 92 million over the last twelve months. Operating cash flow is extremely seasonal: USD 19 million and USD 33 million in the second and third quarters of 2025, USD 1,139 million in the fourth, after an outflow of USD 721 million in the first, and the first-quarter 2026 outflow was larger at USD 827 million. Dividends of USD 300 million in 2025 exceeded free cash flow by USD 219 million before the suspension.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-05-06_exhibit991pressrelease0331.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-08-03_exhibit991pressrelease0630.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_exhibit991pressrelease0930.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C43; calculation C36; calculation C22; calculation C46

The June 2026 refinancing cut maturity risk and, unless the older notes share the security, raised loss given default for unsecured creditors. It replaced the USD 3,500 million unsecured revolver with a USD 2,000 million asset-based facility and USD 2,000 million of second-lien notes, USD 4,000 million of secured capacity, at USD 153.75 million a year of coupons on the notes. Whether the older notes share that security is not established, Moody's and Fitch cut their ratings again to Ba3 and BB- in the second quarter, and the executed documents were not supplied, so remaining basket capacity is unmeasured.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-03-31_whr-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 38; calculation C14; calculation C15

Financial policy is now creditor-supportive, and sponsor and governance risk is Medium, but both rest on documents not supplied. No sponsor is named, the common dividend is suspended, no shares were repurchased, USD 1,081 million of equity was raised and the preferred costs about USD 48.88 million a year in cash; the proxy statement and the executed debt documents that would show board independence and restricted-payment capacity are missing.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C12; calculation C16

Claims outside debt and an intangible-heavy asset base weaken recovery support. Brazil tax items of USD 806 million are outstanding or unreserved, Brazil customer-credit guarantees were USD 320 million, goodwill and other intangibles of USD 5,649 million exceed stockholders' equity by USD 1,934 million, and the retained equity stakes with a fair value of USD 674 million are the identifiable assets that could be monetised.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C20; calculation C19; calculation C21; calculation C17
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against a weak view is that management has pulled most levers early and the operating cash flow target has held at about USD 700 million through three releases. Dividends are suspended, USD 1,081 million of equity was raised, nothing was drawn on the asset-based facility, maturities are cleared until 2028 on management's statement, ongoing EBIT margin has risen each quarter, and the 25% tariff on imported appliances favours a business that makes about 80% of the major appliances it sells in the United States. Small domestic appliances earned an 18.6% EBIT margin in the third quarter and October orders in the United States were reported up about 40%.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; EX-99.1_2026-08-03_exhibit991pressrelease0630.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_exhibit991pressrelease0930.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; calculation C12; calculation C24

The view would improve if fourth-quarter operating cash flow reaches the guided USD 1,526 million and net debt ends below USD 4,500 million, if availability under the borrowing base is shown to cover a first-quarter outflow of the 2026 size, and if the executed documents show that the older notes share the new security. It would worsen if the fourth-quarter inflow falls toward last year's USD 1,139 million, which leaves net debt about USD 260 million above the target, if margin guidance is cut again, if availability nears the level at which the fixed charge test springs, or if distributions resume before net debt falls.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-26_exhibit991pressrelease0930.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; calculation C24; calculation C22; calculation C29; calculation C45
### Limitations

- Borrowing-base availability, letters of credit under the asset-based facility and the facility maturity are not stated, so the liquidity conclusion rests on committed amounts that could overstate what can be drawn.
- The fourth-quarter figures are derived from guidance stated as approximate round numbers, so the implied cash inflow, the implied earnings and the gap to the net debt target are approximate.
- No peer, sector or market data were supplied, so the view that the business profile is adequate rests on the issuer's own disclosure and cannot be set against typical leveraged-credit issuers.

- The issuer states no EBITDA, so leverage rests on EBITDA built from statement lines that includes one-offs worth USD 129 million over the last twelve months, and the leverage conclusion would look worse on the measure that excludes them.

- The proxy statement and executed debt documents were not read, so the governance direction, restricted-payment capacity and the ranking of the older unsecured notes are not established and could change the view of loss given default.
- A recovery value, legal capacity and covenant headroom are not assessed here, so no conclusion on loss given default, basket capacity or compliance is drawn.
### Strengths and weaknesses

The main strength is near-term liquidity: cash of USD 1,103 million and undrawn facilities of USD 2,193 million give USD 3,296 million before any borrowing-base cap, against USD 14 million of debt due within twelve months, and management states that maturities are cleared until 2028.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; EX-99.1_2026-08-03_exhibit991pressrelease0630.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_exhibit991pressrelease0930.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C9

A second strength is a scaled, branded and largely domestic manufacturing base that benefits from import tariffs: about 80% of the major appliances sold in the United States are made there, a 25% tariff applies to imported appliances, and small domestic appliances earned an 18.6% EBIT margin in the third quarter.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 64; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_exhibit991pressrelease0930.htm.jsonl, page 1

A third strength is a financial policy that has turned supportive: the common dividend is suspended, USD 1,081 million of net equity was raised, and the mandatory convertible preferred converts into equity in February 2029.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C12

The main weakness is leverage and cash conversion: net debt is 7.10x EBITDA, free cash flow was negative USD 92 million over the last twelve months, and the net debt target depends on a fourth-quarter operating cash inflow of USD 1,526 million.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3; calculation C10; calculation C24

A second weakness is concentration and margin pressure: MDA North America is 65.43% of sales, Lowe's is about 15% of sales and about 44% of receivables, and the North American EBIT margin was 2.0% over nine months against 5.6%.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 47–49; calculation C18

A third weakness is ranking and asset quality: USD 4,000 million of secured capacity sits ahead of unsecured claims on the main asset pool unless the older notes share it, Moody's and Fitch rate the debt Ba3 and BB-, and goodwill and other intangibles exceed equity by USD 1,934 million.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53; calculation C14; calculation C21

A fourth weakness is claims outside debt: Brazil tax items of USD 806 million, Brazil customer-credit guarantees of USD 320 million and USD 578 million of bank guarantees, letters of credit and surety bonds.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 58; calculation C20; calculation C19; calculation C47

### Company description

Whirlpool makes and sells major home appliances (laundry, refrigerators and freezers, cooking and dishwashing) and small domestic appliances led by the KitchenAid stand mixer, under brands led by Whirlpool and KitchenAid. It sells mainly to retailers, distributors and builders and directly to consumers, and most products are not sold under long-term contracts. North America is the core: MDA North America was 65.43% of 2025 net sales, the United States alone 65.06%, and Lowe's about 15% of sales and about 44% of receivables; Latin America was 21.08%, with Brazil 15.46%, and small domestic appliances 7.14%. The portfolio has narrowed through the 2024 exit from Europe and the Middle East and North Africa, the cut of the India stake to about 40% in November 2025 and the sale of the last 25% of Beko Europe in June 2026.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 4–8; 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13

Demand is cyclical and discretionary and moves with housing and consumer confidence, so cash-flow visibility is low outside the seasonal pattern of a first half of cash outflows and a fourth quarter of cash inflow. That pattern supports debt service mainly in the fourth quarter, and it makes refinancing confidence depend on a recovery in North American earnings rather than on contracted revenue.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; EX-99.1_2026-05-06_exhibit991pressrelease0331.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_exhibit991pressrelease0930.htm.jsonl, page 1
### Ownership and group structure

Whirlpool is a widely traded public company with no sponsor or controlling holder named; the proxy statement that would show holders above 5% and the board was not supplied, so who controls the votes is not established. Financial policy has tightened: the common dividend is suspended, no shares were repurchased in 2025 or the first nine months of 2026, USD 1,081 million of net equity was raised in February, and the preferred costs about USD 48.88 million a year in cash until it converts in February 2029. Sponsor and governance risk is assessed as Medium because distributions exceeded free cash flow in 2025, covenant relief was needed in May 2026 and secured debt now ranks ahead of unsecured claims, set against supportive actions since.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C12; calculation C16

The asset-based facility and the second-lien notes are guaranteed by the domestic and Canadian subsidiaries that are obligors under the facility. The filings name no foreign guarantor and no guarantor-only statements were supplied, so the share of earnings and assets outside the guarantee group is not established, although Latin America is 21.08% of sales and manufacturing sits partly in Mexico and Brazil. Claims of creditors of subsidiaries outside the group, such as the banks behind the USD 320 million of Brazil customer-credit guarantees, rank ahead of the parent's creditors for the assets those subsidiaries hold.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C19
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is cyclical, discretionary, concentrated and not contractual. Volume is the dominant driver: MDA North America sales fell 8.3% in the third quarter and 5.9% in nine months on soft industry demand, and the first-quarter release describes a recession-level industry decline in the United States after consumer confidence collapsed in late February and March, which it attributes to the war in Iran. Price and mix swing the result: unfavourable in the first quarter, when the Supreme Court tariff ruling and expected refunds disrupted industry pricing, favourable in the third quarter after the largest price increase in a decade, with a further 7% increase effective in the fourth quarter and up to 10% in Latin America.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 48–49; EX-99.1_2026-05-06_exhibit991pressrelease0331.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_exhibit991pressrelease0930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 47–48

Currency flatters Latin America, where nine-month sales rose 6.6% but fell 0.9% excluding currency, and customer credit is a risk after the Casas Bahia bankruptcy. Management's industry outlook is about 5% lower for North America, 5% to 7% higher for Latin America and flat for small domestic appliances. The credit consequence is that revenue offers little visibility, the price increases must hold against import competitors that pre-loaded inventory and may discount, and a fourth-quarter miss would flow straight into the cash target.
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Margins have not been defended under volume pressure, tariffs and cost inflation. Gross margin fell to 13.08% over the last twelve months from 15.37% in 2025, and to 12.7% in nine months from 15.8%; MDA North America lost 63.82% of each lost sales dollar in EBIT, and its EBIT margin ran 0.3%, 2.7% and 3.0% across the three quarters against 4.9% in 2025. The cost base carries tariffs on steel, aluminum, copper and imported components, fuel and logistics inflation and the fixed cost of 20 manufacturing locations, and the split between fixed and variable cost is not disclosed.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 48–49; EX-99.1_2026-05-06_exhibit991pressrelease0331.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; EX-99.1_2026-08-03_exhibit991pressrelease0630.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_exhibit991pressrelease0930.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 64; calculation C40; calculation C41

Mitigants are real: about 80% of the major appliances sold in the United States are made there and about 96% of the steel used there is domestic, cost take-out was about USD 200 million in 2025 and over USD 150 million is targeted for 2026, restructuring charges were USD 108 million in nine months with about USD 170 million expected for the year, and the Supsa plant closes by the second quarter of 2027. The credit consequence is that operating leverage is high on the way down, cost actions spend cash before they save it, and EBITDA of USD 810 million has little room for another volume shock.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 51; EX-99.1_2026-05-06_exhibit991pressrelease0331.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-03_exhibit991pressrelease0630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51; calculation C2
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

EBITDA has not converted into cash. Capital expenditures were USD 389 million in 2025, 2.51% of sales and 115.09% of depreciation and amortisation, and about USD 400 million is guided for 2026, so capex offers little flexibility without hurting a product refresh that moved more than 30% of the North American portfolio in 2025. Free cash flow was 6.89% of EBITDA in 2025 after 80.67% in 2024 and negative USD 92 million over the last twelve months, after cash interest of USD 350 million in 2025 and restructuring cash costs that run into 2027.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-03-31_whr-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; calculation C42; calculation C43; calculation C10

Working capital swings with the season, from an operating outflow of USD 721 million in the first quarter of 2025 to an inflow of USD 1,139 million in the fourth, helped by supplier finance of USD 650 million at 2026-09-30, so year-end cash is a seasonal peak. The credit consequence is that debt service depends on a fourth-quarter release that must be larger in 2026 than in 2025 on lower earnings, and that the preferred dividend of USD 48.88 million a year comes out of the same cash now that the common dividend is suspended.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-05-06_exhibit991pressrelease0331.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_exhibit991pressrelease0930.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation C22; calculation C24; calculation C16
### Porter's five forces

Competitive rivalry is intense and rising in the credit-relevant way: BSH, Electrolux, Haier, Hisense, LG, Mabe, Midea, Panasonic and Samsung are expanding beyond their footprints, foreign competitors pre-loaded finished inventory ahead of tariffs, and expected refunds after the tariff ruling encouraged discounting. This puts the 7% and up to 10% price increases at risk and with them the EBITDA recovery.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 64; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_exhibit991pressrelease0930.htm.jsonl, page 2

Buyer power is high. Large trade customers can change volume among suppliers, most products are not sold under long-term contracts, Lowe's was about 15% of sales and about 44% of receivables, and the Casas Bahia bankruptcy cost USD 54 million in the third quarter, so one customer's volume or failure moves cash directly.

Supplier power is moderate: dual sourcing and scale limit single-supplier risk, but tariffs raised steel, aluminum and copper cost and supplier finance of USD 650 million at terms of 120 to 180 days funds part of payables. The threat of new entrants is moderate, because established foreign brands already compete through imports and direct-to-consumer and online channels lower the cost of reaching consumers; the threat of substitutes is low for core appliances, with no substitute evidenced in the files.
### PEST analysis

Political and regulatory factors are material because they move cost and price directly. The Supreme Court invalidated the emergency-powers tariffs in February 2026, with about USD 50 million of tariff recovery and mitigation in the first quarter; a 25% Section 232 tariff on imported appliances followed in April, and Section 301 tariffs took effect in July, the latter subject to legal challenge. Energy-efficiency standards and some local bans on gas cooking appliances add redesign cost and mix risk.

Economic factors matter through consumer confidence and housing-linked demand, which the first-quarter release links to a recession-level industry decline, through Latin American currency, and through the Selic-based interest that accrues on Brazil tax assessments. Social and technological factors matter less to credit: online and direct-to-consumer channels and connected products, with over 100 new products introduced in 2026, support share but do not change cash flow within the debt horizon.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-05-06_exhibit991pressrelease0331.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 47–48
### SWOT analysis

Strengths that support credit are liquidity of USD 3,296 million before any borrowing-base cap, no maturity before 2028 on management's statement, a scaled branded franchise that is largely made in the United States, a small domestic appliance segment earning an 18.6% EBIT margin, and a supportive financial policy since the second half of 2025.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_exhibit991pressrelease0930.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C9

Weaknesses that constrain credit are leverage of 7.10x EBITDA, cash conversion of 6.89% of EBITDA in 2025, concentration in MDA North America and one customer, an intangible-heavy asset base with goodwill and other intangibles USD 1,934 million above equity, and claims outside debt of at least USD 806 million in Brazil tax items alone.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3; calculation C43; calculation C21; calculation C20

Opportunities that could improve credit are price increases and USD 150 million of cost take-out restoring margin, the 25% tariff on imported appliances shifting share to domestic production, monetisation of stakes with a fair value of USD 674 million, and conversion of the preferred into equity in February 2029. Threats that could weaken it are a further decline in North American industry demand, competitor discounting, customer failures such as Casas Bahia, a reversal or legal defeat of tariffs, and further rating downgrades.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 64; EX-99.1_2026-05-06_exhibit991pressrelease0331.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-03_exhibit991pressrelease0630.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C17
### Key strengths and weaknesses

Ranked strengths: first, liquidity of USD 3,296 million against USD 14 million of debt due within twelve months, which lowers near-term default risk; second, equity of USD 1,081 million raised with the dividend suspended, which cut the revolver and slowed net debt growth; third, a largely domestic manufacturing base facing a 25% import tariff, which supports price realisation; fourth, a small domestic appliance segment at an 18.6% EBIT margin, which cushions group EBIT; fifth, monetisable stakes with a fair value of USD 674 million, which give a buffer for debt reduction.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_whr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 64; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_exhibit991pressrelease0930.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C9; calculation C12; calculation C17

Ranked weaknesses: first, net debt of 7.10x EBITDA with negative free cash flow, which raises refinancing and default risk; second, dependence on a fourth-quarter inflow of USD 1,526 million, which makes the net debt target a working-capital outcome; third, concentration in North America and one customer, which ties cash to one demand cycle; fourth, secured capacity of USD 4,000 million ahead of unsecured claims, which raises loss given default for unsecured creditors unless they share the security; fifth, claims outside debt of at least USD 806 million in Brazil tax items, which could absorb liquidity.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3; calculation C24; calculation C14; calculation C20

### Financial profile and credit quality

The main credit supports are liquidity and the absence of near-term maturities, a financial policy that now protects creditors, scale and brands, and tariff protection for domestic manufacturing. The main constraints are leverage of 7.10x EBITDA, negative free cash flow over the last twelve months, margin compression in North America, a heavy dependence on one seasonal quarter and a secured structure that ranks ahead of the older unsecured notes unless they share the security. Free cash flow stability and margin stability are the weakest dimensions, and liquidity and refinancing access in the near term the strongest, with ratings of Ba3 at Moody's, BB- at Fitch and BB with a negative outlook at S&P limiting market access.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53; calculation C3; calculation C10

The trend is down on earnings and cash conversion and flat on liquidity: reported EBITDA fell from USD 1,176 million in 2025 to USD 810 million over the last twelve months, net debt fell only USD 102 million despite the equity raise, and sequential margin gains in 2026 have not reversed the year-on-year decline. Missing datapoints are the borrowing-base availability and letters of credit, the instrument-level debt after June 2026, cash interest paid in 2026, the executed debt documents, the proxy statement and any peer or market data.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C6; calculation C11
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over 12 to 24 months the decisive events are the fourth-quarter 2026 cash release, the first-quarter 2027 seasonal outflow and the delivery of price and cost actions that management says will drive improvement in 2027, while it also says the pace of recovery is slower than expected. Maturities are cleared until 2028 on management's statement, so refinancing risk is a 2028 question that depends on whether leverage is falling by then. Over three to five years the second-lien notes fall due in 2031 and 2034, the preferred converts in February 2029 and the Supsa closure completes the footprint plan, so the credit's medium-term path depends on rebuilding EBITDA toward the USD 1,176 million of 2025.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-03-31_whr-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 31; EX-99.1_2026-08-03_exhibit991pressrelease0630.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_exhibit991pressrelease0930.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; calculation C24; calculation C6

Sector tailwinds are tariff protection for domestic production and price increases that competitors also need; sector headwinds are soft North American demand, import discounting and raw material, fuel and logistics inflation. Company tailwinds are cost take-out, small domestic appliance growth and monetisable stakes; company headwinds are the concentration in one customer, the Latin American customer failure, the restructuring cash cost and the ranking of secured debt.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 47–49; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 64; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_exhibit991pressrelease0930.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Downside scenario

The scenario that matters is a repeat of the 2026 pattern into the fourth quarter and the first half of 2027. The initiating condition is North American industry demand staying about 5% below the prior year while import competitors keep discounting, so the 7% price increase is partly given back. The first operational break is the fourth quarter: sales fall short of the about USD 4,033 million that guidance implies and ongoing EBIT misses the USD 87 million to USD 116 million, while inventory has already been cut once this year.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-26_exhibit991pressrelease0930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 58; EX-99.1_2026-05-06_exhibit991pressrelease0331.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C31; calculation C33

The financial transmission is that operating cash flow lands near the USD 1,139 million of the fourth quarter of 2025 instead of USD 1,526 million and free cash flow near USD 989 million, so net debt ends 2026 near USD 4,760 million, USD 260 million above the target, and even net debt at the target would be 5.56x the current EBITDA of USD 810 million, so a miss leaves leverage higher still. The first quarter of 2027 then repeats a seasonal outflow of USD 721 million to USD 827 million, which liquidity of USD 3,296 million covers 3.99 times, but the borrowing base shrinks with inventory and receivables, so availability against the springing test level of the greater of 10% of the line cap and USD 135 million becomes the observable trigger.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C22; calculation C24; calculation C23; calculation C29; calculation C30; calculation C44; calculation C45

Management levers are capex held near USD 400 million, cost take-out of over USD 150 million, working capital, sales of stakes worth USD 674 million, which may trigger offers to buy notes at 100% for certain asset-sale proceeds, further sale-leasebacks, and accrual rather than payment of preferred dividends. The liquidity buffer looks sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis through 2027 on the stated figures, because no maturity falls before 2028 on management's statement, but not sufficient to deleverage, so the pressure falls on refinancing confidence and on the loss given default of unsecured creditors if the secured claims are drawn.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_whr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 65; EX-99.1_2026-05-06_exhibit991pressrelease0331.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-03_exhibit991pressrelease0630.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C17

### Overall credit view

Overall, Whirlpool presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, brands, domestic manufacturing behind a 25% import tariff and a small domestic appliance segment earning an 18.6% EBIT margin, but credit quality is constrained by leverage of 7.10x EBITDA, negative free cash flow, concentration in North America and one customer, and secured debt that ranks ahead of the older unsecured notes unless they share it. Cash-flow durability appears weak due to a first half of outflows, a fourth-quarter release that must reach USD 1,526 million and margins that have not yet recovered. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on delivery of the fourth-quarter cash inflow, the recovery of North American margins in 2027 and ratings of Ba3 at Moody's, BB- at Fitch and BB with a negative outlook at S&P. The primary downside path is a fourth-quarter shortfall that leaves net debt near USD 4,760 million, a seasonal first-quarter outflow on a shrinking borrowing base and a springing covenant that warns late. Further analysis would require borrowing-base availability, the executed debt documents, the proxy statement, instrument-level debt after June 2026, cash interest paid in 2026 and peer data.

## Gaps

- Borrowing-base availability and letters of credit under the asset-based facility, and its maturity date, are not stated, so the liquidity of USD 3,296 million may overstate what can be drawn and the distance to the springing covenant cannot be measured. Severity: High. Action: obtain the latest borrowing base certificate and the executed credit agreement.

- The executed asset-based credit agreement, the second-lien indenture and the certificate of designations were not supplied, so basket capacity, the covenant levels other than the springing fixed charge test and the ranking of the older unsecured notes are not established. Severity: High. Action: obtain the exhibits to the Form 8-K of June 16, 2026 and the older indentures.

- The fourth-quarter 2026 result is not yet reported, so the implied cash inflow, earnings and net debt are derived from approximate guidance. Severity: High. Action: obtain the fourth-quarter release when published.

- No cash interest paid is printed for any 2026 period and no instrument-level debt table is printed after June 2026, so interest cover is stated for fiscal years only and the maturity profile after the refinancing rests on management's statement. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain 2026 supplemental cash flow disclosures and a debt schedule at 2026-09-30.

- No peer, sector or market data and no rating agency reports were supplied, so the business profile cannot be compared with typical leveraged-credit issuers and market access cannot be assessed beyond the issuer's own statements. Severity: Medium. Action: supply a peer set and agency reports.
- The proxy statement was not supplied, so board independence, holders above 5% and related-party controls are not established. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the 2026 proxy statement.

- The split between fixed and variable cost and the sales split by product category are not disclosed in the text read, so operating leverage is judged only from reported margin changes. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the annual report chart data and any cost disclosure.

- The issuer states no EBITDA, so EBITDA is built from statement lines and includes one-offs worth USD 129 million over the last twelve months. Severity: Low. Action: obtain an issuer adjusted EBITDA reconciliation if one exists.

- Supplier finance at year-end 2025 is 763 in the annual report and 772 as the opening balance in the 2026 quarterly reports, so the trend in that funding float is stated from the nearer figure. Severity: Low. Action: ask the issuer which balance stands.
- The S&P rating after February 2026 and the dates and outlooks of the second-quarter 2026 Moody's and Fitch downgrades are not stated. Severity: Low. Action: obtain current agency reports.
- Recovery value, legal capacity, covenant headroom and relative value are outside this assessment and are not concluded. Severity: Low. Action: none within this report.
